title: From Burned Attempts to Safe Testing: A Kid-Task Sandbox | vitalii.no
description:
Checking whether a task set actually worked meant playing it for real — which wrote to the child's real task rows, fired the gate logic, and burned their one real attempt. There was no way to test a fix without risking a kid's actual progress. Parents also found the read-aloud voice too fast, with no way to judge a new speed before it was saved for everyone.

A new admin Test tab lets the admin pick a child and replay their real tasks in a sandbox: nothing is written to the real task data, no gate logic fires, and nothing is logged. Tested task sets are flagged so they can be regenerated cleanly afterward. Alongside it, a speech-speed slider controls the read-aloud voice directly, saved per child and paired with a Listen button that speaks a sample line at the chosen setting, so a parent can hear the change before committing to it.

The result: a task set can now be replayed and audited end to end without touching a single real record, and a parent can dial in and audibly test a voice speed — from half speed up to 1.3x — before it's saved system-wide. Both were previously impossible without risking real kid data.
